passage:
The first fire drill of the year was messy. Some students talked. Others walked too slowly. One class went to the wrong place.
After the drill, the principal did not scold everyone immediately. Instead, she asked teachers and students to list what went wrong.
They found three problems: unclear signs, noisy lines, and students who did not know where to stand. The school fixed the signs and practiced again the next week.
The second drill was much better.
Students understood that drills were not games, but they were also not only rules. They were practice for a moment when clear action might keep people safe.
A mistake during practice is useful if people learn before real danger comes.
